issues.legal_issue: An order deciding an application to set aside an execution auction sale determines substantive rights and is a judgment appealable under the applicable Letters Patent clause.
material_facts: A judgment-debtor applied to set aside an execution auction sale in which the decree-holder had become the purchaser.
A single judge allowed the application, thereby affecting the purchaser’s right to have the sale confirmed and the judgment-debtor’s right to have the sale set aside.
The purchaser challenged the single judge’s order by a Letters Patent appeal.
issues.conclusion: The order in the sale-setting-aside proceeding was a judgment, and a Letters Patent appeal against it was maintainable.
issues.legal_principle: Under clause 10 of the Allahabad High Court Letters Patent, an order is a judgment where it determines a substantive right or liability, even if it does not terminate the underlying suit. An order under Order XXI, rule 90, affects the purchaser’s right to confirmation under rule 92 and the judgment-debtor’s right to seek the sale’s setting aside. The Court relied on the rights-based approach discussed in Justices of the Peace for Calcutta v. Oriental Gas Co. and State of Uttar Pradesh v. Vijay Anand Maharaj, and distinguished the transfer order considered in Asrumati Debi v. Kumar Rupendra Deb Raikot; it also considered Standard Glass Beads Factory v. Shri Dhar.

predicates.execution_sale_challenge_proceeding: The order arose in a proceeding challenging an auction sale conducted to enforce a judgment or decree.
predicates.order_determines_substantive_sale_rights: The order determined the purchaser’s right to confirmation of the sale or the debtor’s right to have it set aside.

issues.definition: When an order in a challenge to an execution sale determines substantive sale rights, an appeal under the applicable Letters Patent is maintainable.

issues.legal_issue: An execution auction sale cannot be set aside for irregularity or fraud unless the applicant establishes injury caused by that irregularity or fraud.
material_facts: The notice for the adjourned auction sale did not specify the hour of sale, although the original proclamation had specified the date and hour.
The judgment-debtor sought to set aside the sale, alleging material irregularity and inadequacy of the price paid by the purchaser.
The judgment-debtor relied on a valuation report prepared without notice to the purchaser or an opportunity for the purchaser to object.

No other evidence was led to establish the value of the property share or that the price was inadequate, and the judgment-debtor did not establish that any inadequacy resulted from the omission in the notice.
issues.conclusion: The sale was not liable to be set aside because the judgment-debtor failed to establish inadequacy of price caused by the alleged material irregularity.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXI, rule 90, as amended by the Allahabad High Court, requires the applicant to satisfy the court that injury was sustained by reason of the irregularity or fraud. Proof of irregularity and injury, including an allegedly inadequate sale price, is not sufficient without a causal connection between them. The Court considered the alleged omission under Order XXI, rule 69, but held that the valuation report, prepared without notice or an opportunity for the purchaser to object, could not establish inadequacy, and there was no other supporting evidence.

rule.if: execution_sale_set_aside_proceeding and material_sale_irregularity and not injury_caused_by_irregularity_proven

predicates.execution_sale_set_aside_proceeding: An applicant sought to set aside an auction sale conducted in execution of a judgment or decree.
predicates.material_sale_irregularity: A material procedural irregularity occurred in the conduct or notice of the auction sale.
predicates.injury_caused_by_irregularity_proven: The applicant established that the irregularity caused injury, such as a reduced sale price.

issues.definition: If an applicant challenges an execution auction sale for a material irregularity but does not prove injury caused by it, the sale is not set aside.
